guide.name: Figma OAuth Setup and Launch Guide
guide.summary: Configure OAuth for Figma file JSON content reading
guide.timeNote: Planning estimate, not a measured setup duration. Assuming existing OAuth callback and Figma account
guide.review: Figma reviews public OAuth apps, private apps don't require review, draft apps are for testing only, and only admins can authorize draft and private apps, while Figma authorizes public apps
guide.scopeNote: file_content:read scope is sufficient for reading file JSON contents, but further scope mapping may be needed for other endpoints

steps.title: Create OAuth App
steps.detail: Go to figma.com/developers/apps, click My Apps, and create a new OAuth app. Enter a name and select a team or organization. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret, and store them securely. [s1]}

steps.title: Configure OAuth App
steps.detail: Go to figma.com/developers/apps, click the OAuth app, and configure it. Select the file_content:read scope, add a redirect URL, and choose whether the app is private or public. [s1, s2]

steps.title: Test Consent Flow
steps.detail: Provide an authentication URL to the user, and have them follow it to review and consent to the scopes. The user must access the authentication URL using a web browser. [s1]

steps.title: Submit Review
steps.detail: If the app is public, submit it for review by Figma. Provide testing instructions, a link to a testing video, and a free trial URL or login credentials if necessary. [s1, s2]

steps.title: Launch Production
steps.detail: Once the app is approved, use the OAuth app to authenticate users and make REST API requests on their behalf. Ensure the app is configured correctly and the scopes match the endpoints used. [s1, s4]

steps.title: Monitor and Update
steps.detail: Monitor the app's performance, and update the scopes or configuration as needed. Ensure the app complies with Figma's API terms and conditions. [s1, s5]', 'owner': 'developer', 'evidence': 'documented', 'sourceIds': ['s1', 's5']}, {

blockers.title: Missing Client ID and Client Secret
blockers.detail: Ensure the Client ID and Client Secret are stored securely and used correctly in the app configuration. [s1]
blockers.resolution: Regenerate the Client ID and Client Secret if necessary, and update the app configuration.

blockers.title: Incorrect Scopes
blockers.detail: Ensure the scopes selected match the endpoints used in the app. [s1, s5]
blockers.resolution: Update the scopes in the app configuration to match the endpoints used.

blockers.title: Public App Review
blockers.detail: Ensure the public app is submitted for review by Figma and approved before launching production. [s1, s2]
blockers.resolution: Submit the app for review and wait for approval before launching production.

blockers.title: Consent Flow Issues
blockers.detail: Ensure the consent flow is working correctly and the user is able to review and consent to the scopes. [s1]
blockers.resolution: Test the consent flow and update the app configuration as needed to resolve any issues.
